header.name: Computational Metagenomics
header.description: Metagenomics is the approach to genomically investigate entire microbial communities (referred to as the microbiome) in diverse environmental niches. Metagenomic data is typically huge in terms of volume and extremely complex given that the genomic content originates from a multitude of diverse microbes. This requires the development and application of specialized algorithms, customized databases and advanced statistical and AI-based analytics to not only understand the community-level composition and systems biology of these microbiomes but also relate these aspects to the phenotypic traits of the corresponding environment. This foundation course in metagenomics will provide a conceptual overview and understanding of the different aspects of metagenomic data analysis, along with practical hands-on training and assignments.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students should conceptually define the steps of the metagenomics approach and distinguish its different variants (marker gene-based approaches, chip-based approaches) and discuss sequencing technologies for profiling the microbiome

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students should be able to define and implement the preliminary steps of metagenomic data analysis, and utilize customized databases and metagenome-targetted genome assembly strategies

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students should be able to list as well as utilize different databases and profiling methodologies for functional annotation and investigate the interaction dynamics in metagenomes

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students should be able to summarize and implement statistical and artificial intelligence based approaches to associate microbiome composition with other host-/environment-level metadata

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Students should be able to describe, list and decide strategies for identifying microbiome level biomarkers and microbiome-based therapeutic strategies in health care and industrial microbiology

lecture_topics: Overview of the metagenomics approach to understand the microbiome and its variants
Different sequencing methodologies for metagenomes along with their advantages and disadvantages
Species-level classification of metagenomic and other microbiome derived nucleotide sequences
Genome-level binning of metagenomic reads and assembly of novel microbial genomes directly from metagenomic data
Strain-level profiling and bio-surveillance using metagenomics
Annotation and prediction of genes, functional pathways and species-level metabolic production in microbiome sequence data
Understanding inter-species functional interactions in microbiomes using multi-sample metagenome data using statistic learning and state-of-the-art network based approaches
Bioinformatic protocols for Host-/Environment-level Integrated OMICs using the microbiome
Biomarker discovery from metagenomic data using statistical learning and artificial intelligence
Other investigations using metagenomic sequence data
Case Studies on real metagenomic data analysis
